Graduate Application Materials
Required materials for Binghamton's graduate application
Before you apply to graduate school at Binghamton University, gather the following materials:
1. Transcripts
Upload scanned copies of official transcript(s) from each college or university you
have attended to the online application. The Office of Graduate Admissions does not
require hard (paper) copies of your official, final transcript(s) unless you enroll
at Binghamton University. If official transcripts are submitted by mail the Office
of Graduate Admissions is unable to return them.
Scanned copies of your official transcript are preferred. Web printouts of your unofficial
transcript are not acceptable. If you are a current or former Binghamton University
student with access to the Binghamton Portal, you may upload the academic transcript available on BU Brain. To do this, go to
the "Student" tab, then "Student Records," select "Online Academic Transcript," perform
the print function, then change "Destination" to "Save as PDF."
Scan and upload the files with care, making sure they are clear, legible and complete.
The graduate admissions committee will receive the files you scan and upload.
Preferred file format is PDF. Other accepted file formats include .doc, .docx, .rtf,
.jpg and .tif.
Check that your transcript shows all of your grades or marks, as well as your degree
type and your degree conferral date. If you are in the process of completing a degree,
submit copies of your most current transcript with your online application.
Cross out or cover your Social Security Number (SSN) prior to scanning your transcript.
Your SSN should not appear on your scanned transcript.
Transcripts for international graduate applicants:
All transcripts submitted to Binghamton University's Office of Graduate Admissions
must be officially translated into English for review. If you earned your degree outside
the United States, note that some international transcripts do not clearly indicate
that a degree was granted. In this case, you must also submit an official (attested)
diploma showing that your degree has been conferred or awarded.
Transcripts from graduate applicants from India:
Binghamton University will accept a provisional certificate of degree as final for
graduate admission purposes. However, if you are admitted, you must provide official
proof of degree completion before registering for courses beyond your first semester.
2. Personal statement
The personal statement is your opportunity to share your talents, experiences and goals that qualify you for acceptance to a graduate program
at Binghamton University. The graduate admissions committee is seeking evidence of
your qualifications and aptitude, as well as your ability to communicate clearly and
professionally.
What to include in your graduate personal statement:
Your reasons for pursuing graduate study at Binghamton University
Your personal background
Your academic history
Your work and internship experience
Your future plans or research goals
Any additional information that may be of special interest and importance to the graduate
admissions committee
Before you begin, view your program's admissions requirements for specific content
and page length/word count. Unless noted otherwise by your program:
Limit your personal statement to two singled-spaced pages.
Use a standard font, such as Times New Roman or Arial.
Proofread for clarity, structure and tone.
3. Resume or curriculum vitae
Your resume or curriculum vitae (CV) is an important part of your graduate application
at Binghamton University. It provides the admissions committee with an overview of your academic background,
professional experiences, research and achievements that support your application.
What to include in your graduate application resume or CV:
Full name and contact information
Educational degrees and certificates
Work and volunteer experience listed in chronological order
Research or teaching experience
Publications or creative works
Awards, grants or fellowships
Professional associations and licenses
Unless noted otherwise by your program, your resume or CV should be a maximum of two
pages in length.
4. Letters of recommendation
The Office of Graduate Admissions generally requires two letters of recommendation
from individuals who can comment authoritatively on your academic achievements and/or
work or internship experience related to your program.
Check your program's specific requirements, as some departments may require three letters of recommendation or additional documentation.
Choosing and preparing your recommenders
Select recommenders who know you well and can speak to your academic potential and
relevant experience
Be sure to give your recommenders enough time to write and submit the letters prior
to your program's application deadline.
When you submit you recommenders' contact information on the online application, they
will receive an email with instructions for uploading their letter. You will receive
an email confirmation when your recommender has uploaded the letter.
You may submit your online application before your recommenders have uploaded their
letters. You will continue to have full access to your recommender list if you need
to send reminders or change recommenders.
Submitting letters of recommendation
The Office of Graduate Admissions strongly encourages all recommenders to submit letters
online to expedite the completion of your application.
If your recommender is unable to submit the letter online, your recommender may mail
the letter directly to the Office of Graduate Admissions; however, you must still
register your recommender on the online application. The letter must be:
sent in a signed, sealed envelope
addressed to the Office of Graduate Admissions mailing address
5. Official test scores
Many graduate programs at Binghamton University require official test scores, such
as the GRE (Graduate Record Examination) or the GMAT (Graduate Management Admissions
Test), to help demonstrate your aptitude for graduate studies.
Although the Office of Graduate Admissions does not establish minimum test scores,
admission is competitive, so strive for scores that strengthen your application.
Check your program's admission requirements to see what test scores are required.
Submitting official test scores
All official test scores must be sent electronically directly from the testing agency
to the Office of Graduate Admissions.
Do not send scores directly to the academic department.
It can take as long as two full weeks for the testing agency to process your order
and deliver your scores to Binghamton University.
Be sure you take tests early enough to provide scores by your program's application
deadline.
GRE
GRE requirements vary by program with some requiring GRE Subject Test scores in addition
to standard GRE scores. View your program's admission requirements for details.
Both the GRE Standard and GRE Home Edition will be accepted.
Submit test scores electronically, using Binghamton University's code: 2535.
To learn more about the test or to register, visit the GRE website.
The GRE offers a Fee Reduction Program for eligible students.
GMAT
Some programs in the School of Management may require GMAT scores rather than GRE
scores. View your program's admission requirements for details.
Submit test scores electronically by selecting "State University of New York (SUNY)
- Binghamton University" from the score delivery menu.
To learn more about the test or to register to take the test, visit the GMAT website.
6. Paid application fee
The non-refundable application fee for Binghamton University is $75 (USD). Some students
may be eligible for an application fee waiver. Information on who is eligible can
be found on our Graduate Student FAQ webpage.
Additional application requirements for international students
All international students applying to a Binghamton University graduate program must
submit additional materials.
